intro.speaker: S1
intro.quote: I’m Sophia. I’m the product lead on the partner portal.

intro.speaker: S2
intro.quote: And I’m Tom. I’m doing the back end. Well, mostly the back end.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Hey, Tom. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yep, loud and clear. Hey, Sophia. How was the weekend?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Short. Way too short. You?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Moving apartments. Don’t ask.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Oof. Okay, I won’t. So, um, quick intro for the recording. I’m Sophia. I’m the product lead on the partner portal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: And I’m Tom. I’m doing the back end. Well, mostly the back end.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Mostly. Okay, so I just wanna go through what’s left before the launch, 'cause it’s getting close. Like, really close.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah. So first thing, the partner team is still waiting on the API docs. They pinged me again this morning, actually.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Ugh, right. Can you get those over to them, like, by Wednesday?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah, yeah. I’ll send them the docs by Wednesday. That’s fine.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Does that include the auth part? They kept asking about tokens.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah, the whole thing, auth, webhooks, all of it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Oh, and while I’m in there, we could also add a dark mode. People keep asking for it, and it’s honestly not that much work. I could just-

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: I know, I know. I’d rather not. Not this release. Let’s keep it tight.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Fair. Fair enough.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Okay, next one, the staging demo. Can you have it up by Thursday?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Thursday. Yeah, Thursday works.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Great, and I’ll book the big room for the client workshop, the one on the fourth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: The one with the projector that never works?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Yes, that one. I’ll book it anyway.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Um, one more thing. The privacy policy page has to be updated before launch. Like, it really has to.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah. No, that definitely needs to happen. Oh, and do we even know if they need single sign-on, SSO?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Honestly, no idea. Nobody’s asked them yet.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Hmm. Okay. Also, uh, the flaky tests in the payment module, I’ll try to look at them this week, but, you know, no promises.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That’s fine. Whenever you can.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Actually, wait, sorry. Going back to the staging demo, Thursday’s too tight. The database migration is gonna eat, like, the whole week. Can we say Monday instead?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Is the migration okay, though? Should I be worried?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Nah, it’s fine. It’s just slow. Lots of data.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Okay. Monday. Yeah, okay. Let’s make it Monday.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Cool. Thank you.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Oh, and I just got a message from the client. They wanna do the workshop online now, so I won’t book the room after all.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: The projector lives another day.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Exactly. Okay, I think that’s everything. Thanks, Tom.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Thanks, Sophia. Talk soon.
